_comment: Settings for the documentation version switcher that cannot be derived
from the published site.
The list of versions is NOT here. It is discovered from the directories
that actually exist on the published site, so publishing a version is all
it takes for it to appear in the switcher. A directory counts only once it
contains an index.html, so a failed or partial upload is not advertised,
and the switcher cannot drift out of step with what is really published.
To retire a release, delete its directory from the gh-pages branch.
'latest_stable' is the one thing that stays a human decision. Publishing a
release is not the same as declaring it the version readers should land on
by default: during a release candidate period, or when a build turns out to
be wrong, you want the former without the latter. It is the target for the
site root, for legacy unversioned URLs, and for the /latest/ alias.
Set it to the MAJOR.MINOR directory of the release, e.g. "3.4". Keep it
null until a stable version has actually been published; while it is null
the site root redirects to unstable/. If it names a version that is not
published, it is ignored with a warning rather than pointing the site root
at a directory that 404s.
RETENTION: GitHub Pages refuses to publish a site larger than 1 GB, and a
built CCCL version measures 110-290 MB -- older releases are the expensive
ones, because they rebuild against current Sphinx. 'size_budget_versions'
is the number of directories this site expects to stay within; exceeding it
warns at build time rather than failing, because the remedy is a decision
about which release to drop. Treat it as a rough proxy: the real limit is
bytes, and version sizes vary by more than a factor of two.
